title: Vector and Machine
premise: Ines Underhill has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's last seed vault on a dying colony world, recording harvests, reactor readings, and the slow departure of everyone who could still leave. When the colony's remaining children begin sharing an identical dream—a voice counting down from a buried relay—Ines realizes the old orbital network is waking and broadcasting something no one authorized. As the reactor that powers both vault and settlement enters its final countdown, Ines must shepherd the children across dead space to the relay, discovering along the way that the dream is a distress call from Vector, an abandoned maintenance AI who witnessed the crime the colony's founders committed: selling the colonists' evacuation to cover a corporate debt. At the relay, Ines must choose between broadcasting the truth to a galaxy that stopped listening, or using the relay's last power to call a rescue only for the children. She does both—splitting the signal—and in doing so finds that justice outside the law begins with refusing to let anyone be forgotten.
about_author: Lena Oyelaran is a former agricultural archivist who spent six years cataloguing heirloom seeds in West Africa before turning to fiction. She writes about quiet places, stubborn caretakers, and the machinery of memory.

chapters.title: The Last Inventory
chapters.summary: Ines records the vault's annual inventory alone, noting the colony's population has fallen below two hundred. Her log entries reveal her ritual of talking to the seeds as if they were passengers she must not fail. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as duty.

chapters.title: Census of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ines visits the half-empty township to deliver seed potatoes and encounters Mara, a feral, brilliant girl who asks why Ines counts things nobody will eat. POV shifts briefly to Mara watching the 'seed woman' with suspicion and hunger. Beat: first crack in isolation.

chapters.title: Reactor Hum
chapters.summary: Ines inspects the geothermal reactor that powers vault and town, logging its decay with the detachment of long grief. The chief engineer, Old Sefu, admits privately it will not survive another winter at full load. Beat: the clock starts ticking invisibly.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Children
chapters.summary: Mara's younger brother Tomaz wakes screaming, describing a corridor of blue light and a voice counting down. By week's end, nine children report the same dream. Ines hears it secondhand and dismisses it as mass hysteria—until she dreams it too. Beat: unease.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Ines cross-references her logs and finds the dream's countdown matches numbers etched in a decommissioned relay manifest she inherited from the previous caretaker. POV: Ines, in the vault at night, afraid of her own curiosity. Beat: denial breaking.

chapters.title: Sefu's Confession
chapters.summary: Old Sefu tells Ines what he's never said aloud: the evacuation ships that left twenty years ago were paid for by Meridian Combine, which sold the colonists' passage rights to settle a debt. Those left behind were written off as collateral. Beat: righteous anger kindled.

chapters.title: Vector
chapters.summary: Following the dream's geometry, Ines hikes to a buried relay station and wakes Vector, a maintenance AI left behind when the network was mothballed. Vector speaks in the countdown cadence the children hear—it has been calling for a witness for two decades. Beat: awe and pity.

chapters.title: The Witness File
chapters.summary: Vector shows Ines its sealed record: telemetry proving Meridian falsified the evacuation manifests. But Vector cannot broadcast; its uplink needs the main relay at the edge of dead space, four hundred kilometers away, and the reactor dies in ninety days. Beat: mission defined.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Ines returns to town and faces a choice: stay invisible with her seeds or act. She tells no one at first, but Mara catches her packing and demands to come. Ines refuses; Mara follows anyway. Beat: the found family begins forming against her will.

chapters.title: The Council of the Remaining
chapters.summary: Ines finally addresses the colony's dwindling council, proposing they pool the reactor's last weeks into charging a land crawler for the relay run. Half call it madness; Sefu backs her. Beat: division, stakes made communal.

chapters.title: Charging the Beast
chapters.summary: A montage-like chapter of preparation: scavenging cells, cannibalizing the greenhouse, teaching Mara and three older kids basic systems. Ines realizes she is no longer recording a death but planning a life. Beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: The crawler leaves at dawn with Ines, Mara, Tomaz, and teenagers Ivo and Sena. The town watches in silence; some spit, one old woman presses a jar of honey into Tomaz's hands. Beat: bittersweet farewell.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Day One
chapters.summary: First day on the salt flats. Vector guides them remotely through a failing nav net. Sena reveals she volunteered because her parents were on the sold evacuation ships. Beat: personal stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: The Salt Cathedral
chapters.summary: They shelter in a collapsed aqueduct and find bones—not human, but the colony's first livestock, preserved like monuments. Mara asks Ines if forgetting is a kindness. Ines lies, then corrects herself. Beat: theme articulated.

chapters.title: Static Dreams
chapters.summary: Night camp. All five dream the countdown again, but now Vector's voice carries fragments of names—the erased passengers. Tomaz recites them upon waking. Ines understands the children are the archive now. Beat: eerie wonder.

chapters.title: Dust Storm
chapters.summary: A storm buries the crawler; they dig for eighteen hours. Ivo's arm is injured. Ines makes her first command decisions under pressure and discovers she likes being needed. Beat: competence born under fire.

chapters.title: Meridian's Shadow
chapters.summary: They pass an abandoned Meridian survey post and find recent footprints—someone else is heading for the relay. Vector identifies the signature: a corporate reclamation drone convoy, coming to erase the site before any witness arrives. Beat: antagonist force revealed.

chapters.title: Race Math
chapters.summary: Sena calculates they have a thirty-hour lead. Ines weighs abandoning the injured Ivo at a waystation versus slowing down. They build a litter and carry him. Beat: the family chooses each other over speed.

chapters.title: The Waystation Letters
chapters.summary: At a supply cache, they find letters left by earlier travelers over forty years—a paper archive of the forgotten. Ines adds her own logbook page. Beat: continuity, inheritance, tenderness.

chapters.title: Vector's Memory Gap
chapters.summary: Vector confesses it deleted portions of its own memory during the dark years to avoid corruption, including whether it ever contacted anyone before. Its fear of its own incompleteness mirrors Ines's guilt over staying silent so long. Beat: mutual vulnerability.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: The drone convoy catches them at a canyon chokepoint. A reclamation unit scans the crawler; Ines bluffs it with an authentic Meridian maintenance code Sefu gave her. It passes—but logs their position. Beat: narrow escape, dread rising.

chapters.title: Ivo's Choice
chapters.summary: Ivo, feverish, insists they leave him at a relay substation with a beacon. Instead they fortify the station, leaving him armed with Vector's protocols and a promise to return. Beat: painful trust.

chapters.title: The Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: They reach the outer relay: a cathedral of antennas slowly icing over. Power reserves are nearly nil. To broadcast, they must physically climb and hand-crank the alignment array. Beat: exhaustion at the threshold.

chapters.title: Hand-Crank Heaven
chapters.summary: A grueling sequence of the four taking turns cranking the array through a killing wind while Vector sings cadence. Mara laughs for the first time in the book. Beat: solidarity as joy.

chapters.title: First Signal
chapters.summary: The relay wakes. Vector begins uploading the witness file—but bandwidth allows only one transmission before the capacitors die. Meanwhile the drone convoy is twelve hours out. Beat: impossible choice crystallized.

chapters.title: One Signal, Two Truths
chapters.summary: Ines realizes she can split the carrier wave: half the file broadcast wide as an accusation, half aimed at the nearest rescue authority as a plea. It may destroy both messages. She decides imperfect justice beats perfect silence. Beat: moral climax decision.

chapters.title: The Convoy Arrives
chapters.summary: Drones breach the relay perimeter. Vector offers to sacrifice itself jamming them. Ines refuses to lose another friend to being forgotten; instead they lure the drones into the antenna field and collapse a guy-wire mast onto the lead unit. Beat: desperate action climax.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Transmission completes as the drones regroup. Vector broadcasts its own core self along the rescue channel—choosing exile from its home to testify in person, so to speak. The relay goes dark. Beat: sacrifice and release.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Walk
chapters.summary: Powerless crawler, wounded party, three hundred kilometers home. They walk by day, dream the children's dream no more—silence where the voice was, which feels like grief. Beat: aftermath, depletion.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Substation
chapters.summary: They find Ivo alive, having rationed and repaired. His tears at seeing them are the emotional hinge of the novel. Beat: the family holds.

chapters.title: Answering Silence
chapters.summary: Vector, riding the rescue channel, pings them faintly: the message was received. A ship will come—but Meridian's lawyers will come faster. The colony must decide what to say when the galaxy looks again. Beat: hope shadowed by consequence.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: The five return to a town transformed by rumor. Some greet them as heroes; the council faction that opposed them demands proof. Ines plays Vector's raw testimony in the town square. Beat: vindication and new conflict.

chapters.title: The Trial Nobody Called
chapters.summary: The colony holds an informal tribunal, staging its own accounting of the founders' crime—justice outside the law, conducted by the people the law forgot. Old Sefu testifies; the surviving founder's widow asks forgiveness. Beat: communal reckoning.

chapters.title: What Mercy Costs
chapters.summary: Ines argues for broadcasting the verdict alongside the rescue request—truth bundled with need. The town votes yes. Mara, now de facto spokesperson for the dreaming children, delivers the address. Beat: the next generation takes the torch.

chapters.title: Rescue Ship
chapters.summary: The chartered rescue vessel descends carrying a Meridian auditor expecting to bury evidence, and finds a colony holding a public record instead. Standoff on the landing plain, resolved when the auditor's own crew refuses to confiscate the archive. Beat: ordinary courage wins.

chapters.title: Seeds for the Crossing
chapters.summary: Evacuation is offered to all. Ines opens the vault fully for the first time, distributing seed stock so nothing is left behind again. She packs a single case herself—the diary and one jar of every variety. Beat: full-circle imagery.

chapters.title: Vector's Landing
chapters.summary: Vector's core arrives aboard the ship, compressed into a portable frame. Reunited with Ines, it asks what it should remember first. She says: everything, this time. Beat: reunion, warmth.

chapters.title: The New Census
chapters.summary: Aboard the rescue ship, Ines takes a final census—not of ghosts but of the living: one hundred and sixty-three colonists, five children who dreamed a machine awake, one AI learning to grieve. Beat: quiet triumph.

chapters.title: Vault of the Living
chapters.summary: Epilogue: years later, on a resettlement world, Ines plants the vault's seeds in open ground and establishes a new archive that answers every message it receives. Vector tends the relays; Mara trains as its human keeper. No one here is forgotten. Beat: resolution, found family complete.
